meanings.usage: 用于描述值得称赞、非常美好或令人印象深刻的事物，可修饰未来、成就、风景等名词
口语和书面语均常用，可表示对事物的赞赏，也可描述辉煌的经历、建筑等
表示用某物在表面来回移动擦拭的动作

meanings.meaning: 障碍（非正式用法，通常用单数形式，the rub 指某个情况中最难解决的问题所在） verb. 擦

meanings.usage: 指一个人区别于他人的固有特征，也可表示对自身所属群体的归属感
用于描述事物或氛围无聊、缺乏趣味，使人感到消沉
后常接介词to，表示对某事物的投入、承诺或责任
用于描述人在没有得到许可的情况下做超出自己权限的事，带有贬义
用于形容人或行为缺乏理智、十分荒唐
指被过度使用以至于失去原有新意的表达或观点，带有贬义
可描述和宇宙相关的事物，也可引申表示极其宏大、不受世俗局限的
除了表示地理位置在郊区，也可引申形容人思想偏狭、平淡无趣，带有贬义色彩
用于描述人过于高估自己，看不起他人，含贬义
用于形容事物是核心的、至关重要的

meanings.meaning: 基础（常用复数形式fundamentals，指某一领域最核心、最基础的规则或事实） adjective. 基础的

meanings.usage: 后常接介词to，表示对某人、某事物的热爱或投入

phrases.usage: 正式用语，用于礼貌地表示自己要做可能稍显冒昧的事，可译为“冒昧做某事，擅自做某事”

examples.en: If there is one -- which I take leave to doubt -- then it is older people who create it, not the young themselves.
examples.zh: 如果确有这样一个问题的话——恕我对此表示怀疑——那也是老年人而非年轻人自己造成的。

examples.en: I take leave to disagree with your view on this project.
examples.zh: 请恕我冒昧，我不赞同你对这个项目的看法。

phrases.usage: 表示开始探讨最核心、最根本的问题，get down to 意为“开始认真处理，着手做”

examples.en: Let us get down to fundamentals and agree that the young are after all human beings -- people just like their elders.
examples.zh: 让我们来认真探讨一下根本问题，先承认年轻人毕竟也是人——和他们的长辈一样的人。

examples.en: Instead of arguing about trivial details, we should get down to fundamentals of the plan.
examples.zh: 我们与其争论无关紧要的细节，不如好好探讨这个计划的根本问题。

phrases.usage: 常用于提醒对方某个容易被忽略的重要事实或理由，可译为“毕竟，终究”

examples.en: Let us get down to fundamentals and agree that the young are after all human beings -- people just like their elders.
examples.zh: 让我们来认真探讨一下根本问题，先承认年轻人毕竟也是人——和他们的长辈一样的人。

examples.en: You shouldn't scold him too much; after all, he is only a child.
examples.zh: 你别太责怪他了，毕竟他还只是个孩子。

phrases.usage: 表示忙于做某事、参与某事，是正式表达

examples.en: For one thing, being a problem gives you a certain identity, and that is one of the things the young are busily engaged in seeking.
examples.zh: 首先，成为问题能给你一种特定的身份，而这正是年轻人忙着追求的东西之一。

examples.en: The researchers are engaged in studying the effect of climate change on local ecosystems.
examples.zh: 研究人员正忙于研究气候变化对当地生态系统的影响。

phrases.usage: 用于描述人或事物带有某种气质、氛围，air在此处意为“神态，气质，氛围”

examples.en: They have an air of freedom, and they have not a dreary commitment to mean ambitions or love of comfort.
examples.zh: 他们有一种自由的气质，不会乏味地投身于卑俗的野心或对安逸的追求中。

examples.en: There is an air of mystery around the old castle at the top of the hill.
examples.zh: 山顶上的那座古堡周围有一种神秘的氛围。

phrases.usage: 指试图通过结交上流社会人士来提高自身社会地位的人，含贬义，可译为“趋炎附势的人，想方设法跻身上流社会的人”

examples.en: They are not anxious social climbers, and they have no devotion to material things.
examples.zh: 他们不是急着往上爬的趋炎附势之徒，也不执着于物质事物。

examples.en: Everyone could tell that she was a social climber who only made friends with rich people.
examples.zh: 所有人都能看出来她是个趋炎附势的人，只和有钱人交朋友。

phrases.usage: 表示“与……形成对比，和……相比”，用于突出两者之间的差异

examples.en: It's as if they were in some sense cosmic beings in violent and lovely contrast with us suburban creatures.
examples.zh: 从某种意义上说，他们仿佛是宇宙的子民，与我们这些世俗庸人形成了强烈而美好的对比。

examples.en: In contrast with last year's cold winter, this winter is unusually warm.
examples.zh: 和去年寒冷的冬天相比，今年的冬天异常暖和。

phrases.usage: 表示“向……求助以获得某物”，是常用的固定搭配

examples.en: He may be conceited, ill-mannered, presumptuous or fatuous, but I do not turn for protection to dreary cliches about respect for elders -- as if mere age were a reason for respect.
examples.zh: 他可能自负、无礼、放肆、愚蠢，但我不会用“要尊重长辈”这种陈腐的套话来为自己撑腰——好像仅凭年龄就值得尊重似的。

examples.en: When you meet difficulties in study, you can turn to your teacher for help.
examples.zh: 你在学习上遇到困难时，可以向老师求助。

grammar.title: 强调句 (Emphatic Sentence)
grammar.structure: It is/was + 被强调部分 + that/who + 句子其余部分
grammar.definition: 用于突出句子中的某个成分（如主语、宾语、状语等），表达强烈语气的句式，常译为“正是……，就是……” 被强调部分指人时可用who/that，指其他事物时只能用that；即使被强调部分是复数，be动词依然用is/was

examples.en: If there is one -- which I take leave to doubt -- then it is older people who create it, not the young themselves.
examples.zh: 如果确有这样一个问题的话——恕我对此表示怀疑——那也是老年人而非年轻人自己造成的。

examples.en: It is your hard work rather than luck that leads to your success.
examples.zh: 正是你的努力而非运气造就了你的成功。

grammar.title: as if 引导的虚拟语气
grammar.structure: 主句 + as if + 从句（从句用相应的过去时态表示虚拟）
grammar.definition: as if意为“好像，仿佛”，当引导的从句表示的内容与事实不符或者是假想的情况时，需要使用虚拟语气 表示与现在事实相反时，从句动词用一般过去时（be动词常用were，所有人称通用）；表示与过去事实相反时用过去完成时

examples.en: It's as if they were in some sense cosmic beings in violent and lovely contrast with us suburban creatures.
examples.zh: 从某种意义上说，他们仿佛是宇宙的子民，与我们这些世俗庸人形成了强烈而美好的对比。

examples.en: He talks as if he knew everything about this field, but actually he is a newcomer.
examples.zh: 他说起话来好像对这个领域无所不知，但实际上他只是个新人。

grammar.title: as 引导的方式状语从句
grammar.definition: as可引导方式状语从句，表示“按照，如同，就像”，说明动作的方式或两者的相似性 用于比较两个动作或情况的相似之处，从句通常是完整的句子，口语中可省略部分成分

examples.en: I accept that we are equals, and I will argue with him, as an equal, if I think he is wrong.
examples.zh: 我认为我们是平等的，如果我觉得他错了，我会以平等的身份和他争论。

examples.en: When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
examples.zh: 入乡随俗。

patterns.pattern: People are always talking about + 名词/名词短语.

original.en: People are always talking about 'the problem of youth'.
original.zh: 人们总是在谈论“青年问题”。

imitations.en: People are always talking about the impact of social media on teenagers.
imitations.zh: 人们总是在谈论社交媒体对青少年的影响。

imitations.en: People are always talking about the best way to keep healthy in modern society.
imitations.zh: 人们总是在谈论现代社会保持健康的最佳方式。

patterns.pattern: There is only one difference between A and B: A... and B...

original.en: There is only one difference between an old man and a young one: the young man has a glorious future before him and the old one has a splendid future behind him.
original.zh: 老人和年轻人之间只有一个区别：年轻人的前面有辉煌的未来，而老人的辉煌未来已经在身后了。

imitations.en: There is only one difference between optimistic people and pessimistic people: optimistic people always look for opportunities in difficulties, and pessimistic people always see difficulties in opportunities.
imitations.zh: 乐观的人和悲观的人之间只有一个区别：乐观的人总能在困难中寻找机会，而悲观的人总能在机会中看到困难。

imitations.en: There is only one difference between regular exercise and occasional exercise: regular exercise brings long-term health benefits, and occasional exercise only provides short-term comfort.
imitations.zh: 规律运动和偶尔运动只有一个区别：规律运动能带来长期的健康益处，而偶尔运动只能提供短期的安慰。

patterns.pattern: I find + 名词 + 形容词.

original.zh: 我觉得年轻人很有活力。

imitations.en: I find reading books about history very interesting.
imitations.zh: 我觉得读历史相关的书非常有意思。

imitations.en: I find the process of learning a new language challenging but rewarding.
imitations.zh: 我觉得学习一门新语言的过程虽然有挑战，但很有收获。

patterns.pattern: Sb may be..., but I do not... -- as if...

original.en: He may be conceited, ill-mannered, presumptuous or fatuous, but I do not turn for protection to dreary cliches about respect for elders -- as if mere age were a reason for respect.
original.zh: 他可能自负、无礼、放肆、愚蠢，但我不会用“要尊重长辈”这种陈腐的套话来为自己撑腰——好像仅凭年龄就值得尊重似的。

imitations.en: He may be inexperienced and make mistakes sometimes, but I do not deny his value to the team -- as if seniority alone means everything.
imitations.zh: 他可能经验不足，偶尔会犯错，但我不会因此否定他对团队的价值——好像资历本身就代表一切似的。

imitations.en: This method may have some small flaws, but I do not reject it completely -- as if there was a perfect solution in the world.
imitations.zh: 这个方法可能有一些小缺陷，但我不会完全否定它——好像世界上存在完美的解决方案似的。

lines.en: People are always talking about 'the problem of youth'.
lines.zh: 人们总是在谈论“青年问题”。

lines.en: If there is one -- which I take leave to doubt -- then it is older people who create it, not the young themselves.
lines.zh: 如果这个问题存在的话--请允许我对此持怀疑态度--那么，这个问题是由老年人而不是青年人造成的。

lines.en: Let us get down to fundamentals and agree that the young are after all human beings -- people just like their elders.
lines.zh: 让我们来认真研究一些基本事实：承认青年人和他们的长辈一样也是人。

lines.en: There is only one difference between an old man and a young one: the young man has a glorious future before him and the old one has a splendid future behind him: and maybe that is where the rub is.
lines.zh: 老年人和青年人只有一个区别：青年人有光辉灿烂的前景，而老年人的辉煌已成为过去。

lines.en: When I was a teenager, I felt that I was just young and uncertain -- that I was a new boy in a huge school, and I would have been very pleased to be regarded as something so interesting as a problem.
lines.zh: 问题的症结恐怕就在这里。

lines.en: For one thing, being a problem gives you a certain identity, and that is one of the things the young are busily engaged in seeking.
lines.zh: 我十几岁时，总感到自己年轻，有些事拿不准--我是一所大学里的一名新生，如果我当时真的被看成像一个问题那样有趣，我会感到很得意的。
因为这至少使我得到了某种承认，这正是年轻人所热衷追求的。

lines.en: They have an air of freedom, and they not a dreary commitment to mean ambitions or love of comfort.
lines.zh: 我觉得年轻人令人振奋，无拘无束。

lines.en: They are not anxious social climbers, and they have no devotion to material things.
lines.zh: 他们既不追逐卑鄙的名利，也不贪图生活的舒适。

lines.en: All this seems to me to link them with life, and the origins of things.
lines.zh: 他们不热衷于向上爬，也不一味追求物质享受。

lines.en: It's as if they were, in some sense, cosmic beings in violent and lovely contrast with us suburban creatures.
lines.zh: 在我看来，所有这些使他们与生命和万物之源联系在了一起。

lines.en: All that is in my mind when I meet a young person.
lines.zh: 从某种意义上讲，他们似乎是宇宙人，同我们这些凡夫俗子形成了强烈而鲜明的对照。

lines.en: He may be conceited , ill-mannered, presumptuous or fatuous , but I do not turn for protection to dreary cliches about respect of elders -- as if mere age were a reason for respect.
lines.zh: 每逢我遇到年轻人，脑子里就想到这些年轻人也许狂妄自负，举止无理，傲慢放肆，愚昧无知，但我不会用应当尊重长者这一套陈词滥调来为我自己辨护，似乎年长就是受人尊敬的理由。

lines.en: I accept that we are equals, and I will argue with him, as an equal, if I think he is wrong.
lines.zh: 我认为我和他们是平等的。

lines.en: FIELDEN HUGHES from Out of the Air, The Listener
lines.zh: 如果我认为他们错了，我就以平等的身份和他们争个明白。

questions.q: How does the writer like to treat young people?
questions.zh: 作者喜欢怎样对待年轻人？
questions.a: He treats them as equals. Even if a young person is conceited, ill-mannered, presumptuous or fatuous, he refuses to fall back on dreary clichés about respect for elders; he accepts that they are equals and will argue with him, as an equal, if he thinks he is wrong.
questions.aZh: 他把年轻人当作平等的人。即使对方自负、无礼、傲慢或愚昧，他也不搬出“应当尊重长者”这套陈词滥调；他承认彼此平等，若认为对方错了，就以平等的身份与他争论。
questions.hint: 答案在课文最后两句：I accept that we are equals, and I will argue with him, as an equal, if I think he is wrong.

questions.q: According to the writer, who really creates “the problem of youth”?
questions.zh: 按照作者的说法，“青年问题”究竟是谁造成的？
questions.a: Older people create it, not the young themselves. The writer even takes leave to doubt whether such a problem exists at all.
questions.aZh: 是老年人造成的，而不是青年人自己。作者甚至表示，对这种问题是否存在他持怀疑态度。
questions.hint: 见第二句：If there is one -- which I take leave to doubt -- then it is older people who create it, not the young themselves.

questions.q: What is the only difference between an old man and a young one?
questions.zh: 老年人和青年人之间唯一的区别是什么？
questions.a: The young man has a glorious future before him, while the old one has a splendid future behind him -- and maybe that is where the rub is.
questions.aZh: 青年人有光辉灿烂的前景在他前方，老年人的辉煌则已成为过去——也许症结正在这里。
questions.hint: 见第四句，注意 before him 与 behind him 的对照，以及 the rub 指“症结、难点”。

questions.q: What does the writer admire in young people, and what do they seem to him to be linked with?
questions.zh: 作者欣赏年轻人的哪些品质？他觉得他们与什么相连？
questions.a: He finds them exciting: they have an air of freedom, no dreary commitment to mean ambitions or love of comfort, they are not anxious social climbers and have no devotion to material things. All this seems to link them with life and the origins of things.
questions.aZh: 他觉得年轻人令人振奋：他们有一种自由的气息，不追逐卑鄙的名利，不贪图安逸，不热衷向上爬，也不一味追求物质享受。这一切似乎使他们与生命和万物之源相连。
questions.hint: 见第七至第十句：I find young people exciting... All this seems to me to link them with life, and the origins of things.

questions.q: Why does the writer call the young “cosmic beings in violent and lovely contrast with us suburban creatures”?
questions.zh: 作者为什么把年轻人称为“宇宙人”，说他们“同我们这些凡夫俗子形成了强烈而鲜明的对照”？
questions.a: Because they appear fresh, free and elemental, untouched by mean ambitions and material devotion, they seem to belong to life itself, while settled elders look like dull “suburban creatures”. The violent and lovely contrast shows he does not treat youth as a problem to be solved but as energy he admires -- which is why he meets them as equals instead of demanding respect merely for his age.
questions.aZh: 因为他们显得新鲜、自由而带原始的生命力，不为卑鄙名利与物质欲望所累，仿佛属于生命本身；而安顿下来的长者却像沉闷的“郊区生物”。这种强烈而可爱的对照说明他不把青年看作有待解决的“问题”，而看作他所欣赏的生命力——因此他平等待之，而不凭年长要求尊敬。
questions.hint: 结合第十、十一、十二句与末尾两句：all this seems to link them with life... 以及 mere age were a reason for respect 的反问语气。

translation:
人们总是在谈论“青年问题”。
如果这个问题存在的话--请允许我对此持怀疑态度--那么，这个问题是由老年人而不是青年人造成的。
让我们来认真研究一些基本事实：承认青年人和他们的长辈一样也是人。
老年人和青年人只有一个区别：青年人有光辉灿烂的前景，而老年人的辉煌已成为过去。
问题的症结恐怕就在这里。
我十几岁时，总感到自己年轻，有些事拿不准--我是一所大学里的一名新生，如果我当时真的被看成像一个问题那样有趣，我会感到很得意的。
因为这至少使我得到了某种承认，这正是年轻人所热衷追求的。
我觉得年轻人令人振奋，无拘无束。
他们既不追逐卑鄙的名利，也不贪图生活的舒适。
他们不热衷于向上爬，也不一味追求物质享受。
在我看来，所有这些使他们与生命和万物之源联系在了一起。
从某种意义上讲，他们似乎是宇宙人，同我们这些凡夫俗子形成了强烈而鲜明的对照。
每逢我遇到年轻人，脑子里就想到这些年轻人也许狂妄自负，举止无理，傲慢放肆，愚昧无知，但我不会用应当尊重长者这一套陈词滥调来为我自己辨护，似乎年长就是受人尊敬的理由。
我认为我和他们是平等的。
如果我认为他们错了，我就以平等的身份和他们争个明白。
title: Youth
subtitle: 青年

lead.question: 作者认为“青年问题”从何而来？他更愿意以什么态度对待年轻人？
lead.warmup: 人们总爱谈论“青年问题”，仿佛青春本身就是一种需要诊治的毛病。这篇选自《听众》杂志的短文却反问：这个问题是谁造出来的？作者回忆自己十几岁时的心理，甚至盼着被当作“问题”，因为那至少意味着一种身份。他不肯用“应当尊重长者”的套话武装自己，而是先弄清青年与长者究竟差在哪里。
goals: 读懂作者如何用反问、强调句拆掉“青年问题”这一伪命题，把握全文立场。
掌握 take leave to doubt、get down to fundamentals、the rub 等本课表达。
辨析 as if 虚拟语气（were）、动名词作主语、may...but 让步结构等语法点。
能就“代际差异”用英语表达自己的看法，并复述作者对年轻人的评价。
lead.summary: 课文开篇就拆解命题：真存在“青年问题”的话，那也是老年人造出来的。作者欣赏年轻人身上的自由气息：不追逐卑鄙名利，不贪图安逸，不热衷向上爬，因此他们与生命和万物之源相连。面对一个也许自负无礼的年轻人，他不搬出尊重长者的陈词滥调，而是承认彼此平等，认为对方错了就以平等身份争个明白。
lead.tips: 牢记 as if 后的虚拟：It's as if they were... 用 were 而非 are，同理 as if mere age were a reason for respect。另外，泛指青年人须用 the young，谓语取复数：the young are after all human beings，不可说 the young is。

exercises.q: 汉译英：如果这个问题存在的话，那也是老年人造成的，而不是青年人自己。
exercises.a: If there is such a problem, then it is older people who create it, not the young themselves.
exercises.note: 强调句 it is...who；the young 用复数。

exercises.q: 填空：Let us get down to ______ and agree that the young are after all human beings.
exercises.note: get down to + 名词，意为“探讨实质”。

exercises.q: 改错：It's as if they are, in some sense, cosmic beings in violent and lovely contrast with us suburban creatures.
exercises.a: It's as if they were, in some sense, cosmic beings in violent and lovely contrast with us suburban creatures.（are 改为 were）
exercises.note: as if 后表虚拟假设用 were。

exercises.q: 句型转换：He may be conceited, ill-mannered, presumptuous or fatuous, but I do not turn for protection to dreary clichés about respect of elders. 改为 although 引导的让步从句。
exercises.a: Although he may be conceited, ill-mannered, presumptuous or fatuous, I do not turn for protection to dreary clichés about respect of elders.
exercises.note: may...but 转为 although 让步句。

exercises.q: 改错：For one thing, be a problem gives you a certain identity.
exercises.a: For one thing, being a problem gives you a certain identity.（be 改为 being）
exercises.note: 动名词短语作主语，谓语用单数。

exercises.q: 填空：They are not anxious social ______, and they have no ______ to material things.
exercises.note: social climbers 与 devotion to 固定搭配。

exercises.q: 汉译英：我认为我们是平等的；如果我认为他错了，我就以平等的身份和他争论。
exercises.a: I accept that we are equals, and I will argue with him, as an equal, if I think he is wrong.
exercises.note: 条件从句用现在时表将来。

quiz.q: 作者说 “which I take leave to doubt”，这句话的意思是什么？
options: I am leaving the argument to others.
I beg to be excused for doubting that such a problem exists.
I have no doubt at all about the problem of youth.
I refuse to discuss the problem of youth.
quiz.note: take leave to do 即“恕我冒昧地做”，婉转表怀疑。

quiz.q: “and maybe that is where the rub is” 中的 rub 在文中指什么？
options: A kind of physical pain.
A piece of wise advice.
The crux of the matter -- the real difficulty.
An old proverb about age.
quiz.note: rub 意为“症结、难点”，与“摩擦”义相关。

quiz.q: 按照作者的观点，“the problem of youth” 究竟是谁造成的？
options: Older people, not the young themselves.
The young themselves.
Schools and teachers of his time.
The newspapers of his time.
quiz.note: 课文用 it is older people who create it 强调。

quiz.q: “It's as if they were, in some sense, cosmic beings...” 中用 were 而非 are，是因为：
options: 作者在叙述过去发生的事情。
他们真的是来自宇宙的生物。
as if 后面在语法上不能接 are。
as if 引导的从句表示与实际情况不同的虚拟假设。
quiz.note: as if 从句常用 were 表示虚拟。

quiz.q: 作者把某些年轻人称作 “anxious social climbers”，这里 social climbers 指：
options: 喜欢登山运动的社交爱好者。
一心攀附权贵、谋求更高社会地位的人。
积极参加社交聚会的人。
从事社会工作的年轻人。
quiz.note: 与 no devotion to material things 并列，含贬义。

quiz.q: 作者主张用什么方式对待年轻人？
options: 用“应当尊重长者”的道理要求他们服从。
尽量回避与年轻人争论。
视其为平等的人，认为他错了就以平等身份与他争论。
把年轻人当作需要解决的“问题”来研究。
quiz.note: 依据末两句：we are equals / argue with him, as an equal。
